[1.6%]{.lit-num .bad}

[Hydrology and water resources: results could be reproduced from the available artifacts for 1.6% of the tested articles, in a sample of 360 articles from 2017.]{.lit-msg}

[Stagge, J. H., Rosenberg, D. E., Abdallah, A. M., Akbar, H., Attallah, N. A., & James, R. (2019). Assessing data availability and research reproducibility in hydrology and water resources. *Scientific Data*, 6, 190030.]{.lit-cite}
:::

::: {.lit-card}
[86% vs 54%]{.lit-num .bad}

[Geophysics: 86% of 200 articles carry a data availability statement; the original data can be reached for 54%.]{.lit-msg}

[Ireland, M., Algarabel, G., Steventon, M., & Munafò, M. (2023). How reproducible and reliable is geophysical research? *Seismica*, 2(1).]{.lit-cite}
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.lit-card}
[2 of 41]{.lit-num .bad}

[Geoscience papers with open R code: rerunning all 41 raised 173 technical issues, and 2 papers ran without any.]{.lit-msg}

[Konkol, M., Kray, C., & Pfeiffer, M. (2019). Computational reproducibility in geoscientific papers: Insights from a series of studies with geoscientists and a reproduction study. *International Journal of Geographical Information Science*, 33, 408–429.]{.lit-cite}
:::

::: {.lit-card}
[2 HPC systems]{.lit-num}

[Climate modeling: the older EC-Earth3 version produced statistically different climates on two computers; the newer version passed the same test.]{.lit-msg}

[Massonnet, F., Ménégoz, M., Acosta, M., Yepes-Arbós, X., Exarchou, E., & Doblas-Reyes, F. J. (2020). Replicability of the EC-Earth3 Earth system model under a change in computing environment. *Geoscientific Model Development*, 13, 1165–1178.]{.lit-cite}
